why_trail.why: Read DESIGN_NOTE.md, CHECKLIST_SCHEMA.md, validate_spine.py in full, and the render_human/directive-rendering region of checklist_engine.py; confirmed the handoff is complete against its own required-fields checklist. Plan: 7-gate TDD build (pure core red/green, probes+CLI red/green, behavioral proof, full verify).

Wrote the full pure-core test file up front (all 5 kinds, compiler defaults, handback contract, claim escalation + rollup, all 9 named spec-shape faults plus one generator-specific extension for artifact-missing-match). Confirmed RED via ModuleNotFoundError -- the only possible red at this stage since nothing is implemented yet.

Implemented CHECK_KINDS, spec_shape_faults (9 named codes + 1 generator-specific extension spec-artifact-missing-match, decided where the note was silent), compile_condition for all 5 kinds, compile_spec (compiler defaults, handback injection on every gate, claim escalation + rollup). All 43 pure-core tests green: env -u SPINE_FILE -u SPINE_SESSION -u SPINE_ENGINE FORCE_COLOR= NO_COLOR=1 python -m pytest -q tests/test_generate_spine.py -k "CheckKinds or CompileQualitative or CompilePytest or CompileScript or CompilePopulation or CompileArtifact or SpecShape or Handback or ClaimEscalation or CompilerDefaults or PureBoundary" -> 43 passed.

Wrote probe+CLI tests: pytest probe (2 VIOLATING/2 INNOCENT), script probe (2 VIOLATING/2 INNOCENT/1 ACCEPTED_FALSE_ALARM -- second-positional add_argument literal is a real, documented limitation from DESIGN_NOTE section 4's own 'first positional argument' wording, plus a never-imports guard and a missing-target fault), population probe (2 VIOLATING/2 INNOCENT/1 ACCEPTED_FALSE_ALARM -- pathlib dotfile exclusion), main()'s 5 exit codes (1 malformed TOML, 2 spec-shape, 3 probe fault, 4 oracle fault via the control pairing, 0 success), --check-only writes nothing, undecidable refuses with no skip flag, and the control pairing itself (compile_spec translates a literal placeholder-shaped script arg VALUE that its own probe does not examine since it only checks -- flags; the oracle's own falsifiable-unresolved-placeholder fault is what actually refuses it -- both halves in one test class). RED confirmed: 27 failed / 1 passed, all AttributeError on the not-yet-implemented probes/main.

Implemented the impure layer: Undecidable dataclass, _probe_pytest (real collect-only subprocess vs min_collect), _probe_script (ast.parse only, never imports, first-positional add_argument literal collection per DESIGN_NOTE section 4's own wording), _probe_population (executes the compiled command string itself -- one implementation), probe_spec dispatcher, and main() with the exact 6-step order/exit-code contract (1 malformed TOML, 2 spec-shape, 3 probe fault/undecidable, 4 oracle fault/undecidable via validate_spine.validate as the literal last statement, 0 success, --check-only writes nothing). Fixed 4 test bugs found while turning green: missing tomllib import, a default TOML fixture whose lone qualitative postcondition self-tripped spec-all-qualitative-postconditions (switched to artifact/user-decision), a duplicate-gate-id fixture that concatenated two full spec headers into invalid TOML (switched to one header, two [[gate]] blocks), and a mistaken dotfile population false-alarm premise -- measured live that this host's pathlib.Path.glob DOES match dotfiles with a bare '*', so replaced it with the real, measured ** semantics gotcha (matches the top level too, not just subdirectories). Full file green: 70 passed.

Added the behavioral proof: render_human shows the handback block on a generated gate (checklist_engine.current() called directly on the in-memory compiled spine dict -- actual rendered text, not a JSON-shape assertion); all three handback verbs (attach, flag-candidate, block) driven against a generated spine, landing exactly where the contract says (gate evidence[], top-level triage_candidates[], top-level blockers[]); and a falsification-floor test in the test_mutation_floor.py style -- the c-escalation injection block is mechanically deleted from a real COPY of generate_spine.py (occurrence-count-verified before/after so the harness itself cannot fake a kill), a throwaway pytest file exercising only that postcondition is run against the mutant in a subprocess and asserted red, and the same run against the unmutated original is asserted green first. All 6 new tests passed on first run (no red/green cycle needed -- exercising already-working code). Full file: 76 passed.

Full declared-mode suite: 2765 passed, 3 skipped, 1121 subtests (baseline 2689 + 76 new, zero regressions). validate_spine --sweep unchanged at 23 fault lines (no shipped template touched). Wiring grep confirms every generate_spine reference is inside its own test file -- built and verified, not yet called by anything else; role specs land at g2 per the handoff's own scope note. IMPLEMENTER_RESULT.md written with full evidence, findings (oracle config_ref-not-json gap restated per DESIGN_NOTE, no shipped-template disagreement found), 7 documented decisions where the note was silent, and workflow feedback (a self-caught, self-corrected false-alarm-fixture assumption about pathlib dotfile globbing that I verified live before shipping).
